papers.title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
papers.summary: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^γ$, where $γ\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $γ$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.

papers.title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
papers.summary: The degree distribution is among the most basic summaries of a network, yet no functional limit theorem for the empirical degree distribution of graphon models has been available, even for dense, bounded graphons, for which only finite-dimensional results were known. We study the empirical degree distribution of sparse $L^p$ graphon models, allowing unbounded kernels and hence heavy-tailed degrees. For graphons whose latent expected degrees have a density, we prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem whenever $nρ_n/\log n\to\infty$ and $nρ_n^{2+β}\to0$, where $ρ_n$ is the sparsity level and the kernel has $2+β$ moments for some $β>0$; the limiting covariance coincides with that of the dense case. Under additional local regularity, we establish a functional central limit theorem on compact intervals in the interior of the support. Under tail regularity and a stronger sparsity condition, we prove that uniformity extends to unbounded intervals. We also show that uniform limits fail at atoms of the degree distribution, for instance in stochastic block models. The analysis rests on an exact multilinear representation of the conditional degree distribution, which identifies its Hoeffding decomposition without Edgeworth expansions, combined with a lattice version of Billingsley's tightness criterion and moment inequalities of Efron-Stein type.

papers.title: On Natural Exponential Families with Log-Affine Generalized Variance
papers.summary: We study natural exponential families whose generalized variance, the determinant of the covariance matrix, is log-affine in the natural parameter. Without any assumption on the natural parameter domain, we show that every such family is regular and that it is Gaussian when its generalized variance is constant. Consequently, a sample of size $n>d$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ comes from a non-degenerate normal law exactly when the conditional expectation of the sample generalized variance given the sample mean is a positive constant. Every non-Gaussian family puts mass on a facet of its convex support, and, as for a Poisson count, its height above that facet takes only integer multiples of a fixed step. More generally, its displacement away from any exposed face that carries mass has nonnegative integer coordinates in a suitable basis. A local inequality between third and fourth cumulants singles out the Poisson--Gaussian families and yields a complete classification of the infinitely divisible ones. Geometrically, a semi-flat Kähler tube, whose potential has constant Hessian determinant, is flat if some multiple of its metric is projectively induced near a point.

papers.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
papers.summary: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.
papers.comment: 47 pages, 9 figures. Includes a six-page technical overview explaining the main ideas and proof techniques

papers.title: Uniqueness and full coverage in $k$-neighbor graphs
papers.summary: We study the number of infinite clusters in the $2dp$-neighbor graph on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, in which every vertex independently selects $\lfloor 2dp\rfloor$ of its nearest neighbors uniformly at random, and one more with probability $2dp-\lfloor 2dp\rfloor$. The model has negatively correlated edges and, for $1\le2dp\le2d-1$, neither finite energy nor insertion or deletion tolerance. We prove that the undirected graph has at most one infinite cluster for every $p\in [0,1]$, and that in the planar case the same holds for forward and strong forward clusters of the directed graph when $p\in[1/2,1]$. We further exhibit a second phase transition: for $p\ge(d+1)/(2d)$ the open cluster of the origin is almost surely the whole lattice, and for $p>(d+1)/(2d)$ any two vertices of a box are connected inside the box of twice the size with probability exponentially close to one. In particular, the percolation function is continuous but not analytic on the supercritical interval $(p_c,1]$. Finally, we prove that the full-coverage phase transition at $p_f = (d+1)/2d$ is of order $2^d$.

papers.title: Bass martingales need not stretch
papers.summary: In classical optimal transport, the equivalence of optimality, convex gradient structure, and cyclical monotonicity is a central paradigm. Known counterexamples to this equivalence rely on carefully constructed costs. In contrast, we show that this equivalence can fail in martingale transport in dimension ${d \ge 2}$: already for the canonical martingale Benamou-Brenier problem and irreducible marginals we have the strict inclusions \[ \text{optimality} \;\subsetneq \; \text{(Bass) convex gradient structure} \;\subsetneq\; \text{martingale cyclical monotonicity}\, . \] However, under the stronger assumption of strict irreducibility, we establish that these three notions coincide. Understanding when the gradient structure guarantees optimality is also of practical relevance, since algorithms based on the Bass gradient representation are used in financial model calibration. All our counterexamples are based on the following phenomenon: for $d\ge2$, there exist two one-step martingales $X,Y$ with the same initial and terminal laws, and a convex function $ψ$ such that \[ 0=\mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[ψ(Y_1)\mid Y_0]-ψ(Y_0)\big] < \mathbb E\big[\mathbb E[ψ(X_1)\mid X_0]-ψ(X_0)\big] <\infty. \]

papers.title: Universality of smallest singular values of random row submatrices and phase retrieval problems
papers.summary: We establish universal logarithmic laws for extreme least singular values of random row submatrices and for the global stability of real phase retrieval near its injectivity threshold. Let $A_m\in\mathbb{R}^{N_m\times m}$ have i.i.d. entries distributed as a centered, variance-one real subgaussian random variable with a bounded Lebesgue density, and suppose $N_m/m\toγ>1$. For integers $0\le r_m\le N_m-m$, let $M_{m,r_m}(A_m)$ be the minimum least singular value over all row submatrices of $A_m$ with $m+r_m$ rows. Writing $k_m=r_m+1$, we prove that whenever $k_m\log m=o(m)$, $(k_m/m)\log M_{m,r_m}(A_m)$ converges in probability to $-h(γ)$, where $h(γ)=γ\logγ-(γ-1)\log(γ-1)$. This covers both fixed and moderately growing surplus. The limiting rate is universal within the stated class of entry distributions. For real phase retrieval from $N_m=2m-1+r_m$ amplitude measurements, let $L_{A_m}$ denote the optimal lower Lipschitz constant of the map $x\mapsto|A_mx|$, with signals identified up to sign, and let $κ_{\mathrm{ph}}(A_m)=\|A_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}/L_{A_m}$ be its scale-invariant global condition number. In the same surplus regime, $(k_m/m)\log L_{A_m}$ and $(k_m/m)\logκ_{\mathrm{ph}}(A_m)$ converge in probability to $-\log 4$ and $\log 4$, respectively. Although these measurements determine every signal up to sign almost surely, the condition number grows exponentially in dimension for fixed surplus and exceeds every fixed power of $m$ throughout the stated regime, with probability tending to one. These conclusions quantify the distinction between uniqueness and uniform stability under measurement noise. All stated limits also hold almost surely on any common probability space, without requiring independence across dimensions.

papers.title: The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
papers.summary: A $(d+1)$-state lattice is the smallest complete one-step approximation of a $d$-dimensional Brownian market. Its centered quadratic increments must lie in the span of the traded innovations. We study the resulting Gamma-to-Delta aliasing through the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)=\mathbb{E}[(ξ^\top Hξ-\operatorname{tr} H)ξ]$, $H\in\operatorname{Sym}_d$, for centered isotropic innovations $ξ$. For quadratic claims this operator is exactly the difference, scaled by $\sqrt{h}/2$, between the lattice's replicating exposure and its price-sensitivity Delta. Applying the lattice replication rule to a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)|^2/4$ relative to ordinary discrete Delta hedging. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete lattices is $\sqrt{d-1}$, uniquely attained by the equal-probability regular simplex. For positive-semidefinite and rank-one unit-Frobenius Gamma classes, the sharp minimax value is instead $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also describe the corresponding orthogonal quadratic residual in nonminimal markets and the leading implementation error for smooth claims.

papers.title: Logarithmic corrections for four-dimensional loop percolation
papers.summary: We study the one-arm probability of the discrete random-walk loop soup on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ at small positive intensity. Using the small-loop crossing and macroscopic attachment estimates of Gao, we prove that the expected capacity of the origin cluster formed by loops contained in a box grows at most as the square of the logarithm of the box radius. Consequently, there are constants $α_0,c,C,β>0$ such that, for $0<α\leα_0$, \[ cαR^{-2}[\log(R+2)]^{βα} \le \mathbb{P}_α(0\leftrightarrow B_R^c) \le CαR^{-2}[\log(R+2)]^2. \] The interval $(0,α_0]$ is strictly subcritical. The upper bound rests on a simultaneous capacity estimate for neighborhoods of loop ranges, followed by an expansion over chains in which sufficiently small intermediate loops have been removed. A deterministic bound on the variation of the surviving scale sequences makes the expansion summable. The positive logarithmic-power lower bound is already known from work of Chang and Sapozhnikov; we give a proof using macroscopic attachments and a layer-cake argument, with constants uniform at small intensity. In particular, the one-arm exponent equals two, and the logarithm of its correction has order $\log\log R$, for every fixed intensity in this interval. We also derive polynomial tail exponent one for the cardinality and capacity of the full cluster, determine their positive moment thresholds, and give an application to random wires.

papers.title: A unified approach to fluctuations of LES of time-dependent generalized patterned random matrices
papers.summary: A unified approach for studying the linear eigenvalue statistics (LES) of generalized patterned random matrices was developed in Kumar, Maurya, Saha (2026). In this paper, as a continuation, we develop a unified method for studying the time-dependent LES of generalized patterned random matrices with independent process entries such as Brownian motion and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We prove that if the limiting moment sequence of the LES of the generalized patterned random matrix with independent standard Gaussian entries is M-determinate, then under some minimal assumption on the link function, the time-dependent LES converges to a deterministic real-valued process.

papers.title: Two-sided estimates for two-point local time tails of branching random walks: a Green function criterion
papers.summary: This paper is devoted to the study of the joint tails of local times at two distinct sites for branching random walks (BRWs). Our principle results establish a general Green-function criterion for two-sided exponential tail bounds with a common spatial factor given by a three-point Green function convolution, and further identify a strict inequality that must be satisfied by the corresponding exponential constants. In particular, we verify this criterion for subcritical BRWs on finitely generated groups, for critical BRWs on non-elementary hyperbolic groups, and for critical BRWs on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d\geq 5$. As applications, we revisit the growth rate of visited sites on spheres in hyperbolic groups obtained by Sidoravicius et al. [Commun. Pure Appl. Math. 2023], and also establish lower bounds for the probabilities of visiting finite sets in Euclidean lattices.

papers.title: Small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation
papers.summary: This paper investigates the small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation with the full velocity alignment source term, which serves as the mean-field equation for the stochastic Cucker--Smale model. Inspired by the idea of Hottovy et al. \cite{Hottovy2015} to rearrange SDEs via integration by parts, we repeatedly perform integration by parts on independent copies of our equation. Then we define a global position correction and a quadratic remainder, both with uniformly bounded tails. Applying the Aldous criterion, we obtain tightness of the position correction, which in turn yields tightness of the position process. Subsequently, using the averaging method on the fast time scale, the quadratic functional can be decomposed into the equilibrium average, local quadratic fluctuations, and exponential transients. Then, the Poisson--Lyapunov equation is employed to prove the convergence of the time integral. Finally, under various suitable assumptions, we obtain the weak convergence of the laws of the approximating processes to the law of the solution of the small-inertia limit equation, along with the identification of the limiting process, and also the convergence rate of strong $L^1$-convergence. The extra noise-induced drift term can be expressed as the solution of a contraction-type Fredholm equation. This paper is complementary to the deterministic particle limit work of \cite{Carrillo2021,Choi2021} .

papers.title: A general technique for explicit quantile representations
papers.summary: This work proves existence of contours independent of probability level for exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities. Explicit constructions cover five broad distribution families and yield a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility using forward functions.

papers.title: An equivalence principle for martingales
papers.summary: We show that any discrete-time filtration can be embedded into a dyadic filtration, realized via a non-classical measure-preserving map. This embedding makes it possible to reduce certain problems involving vector-valued martingales to the case of Haar martingales. Some applications of this result will also be discussed.

papers.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
papers.summary: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. No standard closed form is available for its remaining life expectancy, which must therefore be evaluated by numerical integration. We show that Siler remaining life expectancy at age $x$ is a Poisson mixture of Gompertz-Makeham remaining life expectancies, that is, a Poisson-weighted average of life expectancies in models with only a constant background hazard and an exponentially increasing senescence hazard. All components share the senescence hazard. Their background hazards increase from one component to the next by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines. The Poisson mean is the immaturity hazard that remains to be accumulated after age $x$. This representation yields an exact series of generalized exponential integrals with a closed-form bound on the truncation error. Replacing the background hazard by its discounted counterpart also gives the Laplace transform of the remaining lifetime. The mixture bounds the life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality: up to a term below the reciprocal of $a_2+b_1$, this loss equals the probability of an immaturity death times the life expectancy with the immaturity hazard removed. In annual Siler fits to Swedish female mortality, we estimate that the loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, which accounts for 15% of the gain in life expectancy at birth over the period.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic limits of the asymmetric Brownian energy process and its dynamic generalization
papers.summary: We prove that the hydrodynamic limit of the asymmetric Brownian energy process (ABEP) is the viscous Burgers equation. We also prove the hydrodynamic limit of the dynamic ABEP which leads to a nonlinear equation for the macroscopic tail-energy potential. Both processes are related to the Brownian energy process (BEP) through invertible, non-local transformations involving discrete tail energies, which can be thought of as the microscopic equivalent of a transformation of Cole-Hopf type. Our main tool is a general micro-to-macro result showing that, under suitable conditions, such microscopic tail transformations induce corresponding transformations of the limiting density profiles. Combining this result with the fact that the hydrodynamic limit of BEP is the heat equation, we obtain the limiting profiles of ABEP and dynamic ABEP as explicit nonlinear transformations of solutions of the heat equation.

papers.title: Critical one-arm probabilities for metric-graph loop soups in dimensions $d\ge3$
papers.summary: We study the critical Brownian loop soup on the metric graph $\widetilde{\mathbb Z}^d$. Using a new unified approach, we determine the one-arm probability up to multiplicative constants in all dimensions $d\ge3$. In particular, at the upper critical dimension $d_c=6$, we show that the one-arm probability is comparable to $r^{-2}(\log r)^{\frac12}$, and moreover, with high probability a box of radius $r$ contains on the order of $\log r$ macroscopic clusters, each with volume of order $r^4(\log r)^{-\frac12}$. For $d\ne6$, we recover the one-arm estimates of Cai and Ding, $r^{-(d-2)/2}$ for $d=3,4,5$ and $r^{-2}$ for $d>6$ (arXiv:2406.02397; Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2025), and the three-dimensional estimate of Drewitz, Prévost and Rodriguez (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2026). Our proof adapts the entropy method of Dewan and Muirhead (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2023) to the loop-soup setting. This yields a renormalization inequality for the one-arm probability, from which we derive the upper bounds. Independently, Rodriguez, Shi, and Zhang (arXiv:2611.05357) have recently used a closely related entropy approach to recover the one-arm estimates for $d>6$ and improve the upper bound for $d=6$. They also announce the same sharp one-arm estimate for $d=6$ in forthcoming work.

papers.title: Retrials in Loss Systems: Mean-Field Analysis, Erlang Bounds, and Power-of-$d$ Comparison
papers.summary: We consider a system of $N$ parallel, homogeneous servers, each with finite capacity $C$. Jobs requiring one unit of capacity arrive according to a Poisson process with total rate $Nλ$ and have exponential service times with rate $μ$. We study a decentralized random--retrial policy with $d$ attempts: upon arrival, a job is assigned to a uniformly chosen server; if the server is full, the job is reassigned to another uniformly chosen server, for at most $d$ attempts; if all $d$ attempts fail, the job is rejected. In the mean-field limit, we prove that the stationary blocking probability is characterized by the unique solution of a fixed-point equation involving the Erlang-B loss function, and we establish global convergence of the fluid model to this equilibrium. We also compare the mean-field stationary blocking probability with the analogous quantity in the power-of-$d$ model under the same parameters $(C,λ,μ)$. For the same $d$, we show, via coupling techniques, that the blocking probability under power-of-$d$ is always less than or equal to the blocking under retrial-of-$d$; but if we consider $d$ and $\tilde d$ with $\tilde d>d$, then the retrial-of-$\tilde d$ policy achieves a strictly lower blocking than the power-of-$d$ policy when $ρ=λ/μ$ is sufficiently large. Moreover we show that for some specific cases, like $C=2$, $d=2$ and $\tilde d=3$, it occurs for all $ρ>0$, not only for $ρ$ sufficiently large. We complement the analysis with simulations that estimate the load level above which retrial-of-$\tilde d$ outperforms power-of-$d$ in terms of blocking.

papers.title: Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes
papers.summary: Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator $\mathrm{L}: \mathcal{S} \to L_2$ specifies both the native Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L} \subset \mathcal{S}'$ of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core $\mathrm{L}^\ast(L_2)$ of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of $\mathrm{L}$ is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.

papers.title: Random waves on sub-Riemannian $SU(2)$
papers.summary: Random spherical eigenfunctions for the Lalplace-Beltrami operator are well understood and their local behavior, after renormalization, is described by Berry's random wave model. In this paper we construct a family of random fields on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, identified with the group $SU(2)$, endowed with a sub-Riemannian structure. These fields are random eigenfunctions for the sub-Laplacian and they are constructed from matrix elements of unitary irreducible representations of $SU(2)$. We prove that the local behavior of such fields is the same as the Berry-Heisenberg random field on the Heisenberg group introduced in [10].

papers.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
papers.summary: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $α$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $α=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.

papers.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
papers.summary: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.summary: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0<β<1$, with $c_β>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: Can a self-sustaining chemical network emerge due to just a few catalysts?
papers.summary: Understanding how self-sustaining chemical reaction networks can emerge from simple molecules is an important question in chemical approaches to the origin of life. Reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) sets provide a mathematical framework for investigating this question. This line of research goes back to the early work of Kauffman on autocatalytic reaction networks and was subsequently developed through the probabilistic framework of Mossel and Steel. Further contributions by Hordijk, Steel, and collaborators extended the theory to more heterogeneous forms of catalysis, including reaction-dependent probabilities or power-law distributions of catalytic activity. We introduce a stochastic model that combines heterogeneous molecular catalytic activity with reaction-dependent molecule-reaction compatibility. By assigning random catalytic weights to molecules and incorporating compatibility through an explicit formulation of catalysis probabilities, our model provides a concrete and flexible setting that captures both sources of heterogeneity while remaining mathematically tractable. We establish novel and general criteria for RAF formation and nonformation. We further demonstrate that classical phase-transition criteria need not remain valid in the presence of reaction-dependent catalysis. For heavy-tailed catalytic weights, we identify and rigorously quantify an additional phase transition. In models with finite-mean catalytic weights, RAF formation and nonformation are governed by a catalytic intensity parameter. For infinite-mean weights, however, we show that RAFs may emerge with probability tending to one even when the catalytic intensity parameter tends to zero.

papers.title: Quantum Adiabatic Theorem under Wiener Noise:Maximal Mean-SquareEstimates
authors: K. K. W. A. S. Kumara
papers.summary: We derive maximal mean-square adiabatic estimates for finite-dimensional stochastic Schrödinger equations with Hamiltonian-proportional Wiener noise. For deterministic $C^2$ Hamiltonians whose eigenvalues have constant multiplicities and do not cross on $[0,1]$, we construct a unitary stochastic adiabatic intertwiner driven by the same Wiener process as the exact propagator. A commutator argument, Itô calculus, and Doob's maximal inequality yield an explicit bound for the expected supremum of their squared operator-norm difference on a selected initial eigenspace. Under uniform coefficient bounds, the physical noise scaling $α=σT^{-γ}$, where $T$ is the total evolution time and $σ\geq0$ and $γ\geq0$ are fixed, gives maximal mean-square error $O(T^{-2}+σ^4T^{-4γ}+σ^2T^{-(2γ+1)})$. Consequently, adiabatic convergence holds for every $γ>0$ as $T\to\infty$, while $γ\geq1/2$ recovers the deterministic $O(T^{-1})$ bound for the root-mean-square maximal error. For fixed nonzero physical noise amplitude, the estimate leaves convergence unresolved.
